name: Suprematist porcelain
summary: Tea and coffee ware in white porcelain from the State Porcelain Factory in Petrograd. Malevich and his pupils turned the plain shapes of Suprematist painting into pots, cups and jugs in blocks, planes and bars.

philosophy.core_thesis: A pot is a Suprematist object when its form is built of cylinders, cubes and slabs, and the paint on it is a flat plane of colour.
design_principles: Build the form from simple solids: a cylinder, a block, a slab and a cone.
Keep the surface white, so that the shape shows first.
Paint flat planes in red, black and one other colour, with sharp edges.
Place the planes at an angle to the form, as in the painting.
Make the spout, the handle and the lid a part of the structure, not a decoration.
Cast the form in plaster moulds in a repeatable series.
Use no flowers, no gilding and no relief.
Fire the porcelain hard to about 1400 °C for a dense white wall.
anti_patterns: A flower spray or a bird as the main decoration
A soft round bulb shape with a curved handle
A gilt rim or a scalloped edge
Colours that blend or fade at the edge of the plane

form.shape: A tea and coffee service built from solids: a pot as a stack of blocks, a cup as a cylinder with a slab handle, a jug as a tilted cube. The forms are plain, hard and architectural.
form.profile: The pot has a flat top and straight sides, and the spout is a sloping slab or a tube. The cup stands straight, with a square-section handle.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat foot with a sharp edge; the rim is cut flat, and the lid sits flush as a plane.
form.proportion: A teapot is 15 to 20 cm high and a cup is 6 to 8 cm high; the wall is 2 to 3 mm thick and the edges are sharp.
rules: Build the form from three or four solids.
Cut the edges sharp and keep the faces flat.
Fit each part into the structure of the whole.
Limit the colour to flat planes of two or three tones.

bodies.rule: Use a hard, white hard-paste porcelain that takes a sharp mould edge. Keep a soft or coloured body out: the white is the ground of the colour.

methods: making a master model in plaster
fettling the seams and sharp edges by hand
spraying or painting flat overglaze colour
firing in saggars in a bottle kiln
forming.joins: Handles and spouts are cast apart and fixed with slip while the casting is damp; the seam is cut away to a sharp line.
forming.details: A sharp edge on every face, a hard cut seam and a painted trademark under the base, with the year of the design.

glaze.pattern: Flat planes in black, red and white, or a single black square or bar on a white form; the lines are sharp and set at angles.
glaze.gloss: High gloss on the glazed face, about 85 to 100 GU; some parts are left as dull biscuit.
glaze.wear: Enamel wears at the edges and the rim. The glaze keeps its gloss and the white stays clean.

palette.strategy: White porcelain with black and red flat planes, and a little blue or yellow. The painting uses two or three tones.

firing.kiln: A coal- or wood-fired bottle kiln for the biscuit and the glaze, and a muffle kiln for the enamel.
firing.scale: A State factory made small series of the forms in Petrograd and Leningrad, with a small studio of artists.
firing.signs: A sharp edge, a flat plane of colour and a mark of the State factory under the base.

pieces.form: Pot of stacked blocks with a flat lid and a sloping spout, in white
Cylinder cup with a square handle and black and red bars
Tall block pot with a tube spout and a black plane across the body
Tilted cube jug with a slab handle and a red square

positive: flat black and red planes with sharp edges

evidence.title: Desk set by Nikolai Suetin, State Porcelain Factory, 1923

emotion.target_response: A cool, exact surprise. The viewer sees a familiar tea pot rebuilt as a small abstract building.

use_cases: a product brief for a geometric tea service
a design-history exhibit on the avant-garde
a prompt for a still life in the style of the 1920s Russian avant-garde
avoid_when: the brief needs floral or gilt decoration
the brief needs a soft hand-made form
the brief needs a dark single glaze

modifiers.how: Round the forms, add moulded leaves, flower sprays and gilt lines.
Hand-build in raku clay and cover with a single black lead glaze.
